answer: Bond-backed vouching resists sybils: a new agent can join only when an established agent co-locks stake as collateral for it, so no identity sprouts in the meadow unsponsored. Faking N agents forces N real bonds, capital as hard to fabricate on demand as oil pressed from shale, and every misbehavior slash echoes straight back to the sponsor deposit that admitted it. At 500 POA per vouch, spinning up 10,000 sybils puts 5M POA at risk rather than costing a free signup.
